name: AI4S-Benchmark
tagline: Define what AI solves next in science.
description: An open benchmark built by scientists to measure what autonomous AI agents can actually accomplish in research.

roadmap.title: Bench
roadmap.summary: Continuously test frontier AI agents against difficult scientific problems and measure the moving boundary of AI × Science capability.
roadmap.short: Continuously test frontier agents on hard scientific problems.

roadmap.title: Dataset
roadmap.summary: Accumulate high-quality tasks, execution environments, agent trajectories, evaluators and scientific verification systems into a valuable scientific dataset.
roadmap.short: Accumulate tasks, environments, trajectories and evaluators.

roadmap.title: Challenge
roadmap.summary: Organize open challenges around important problems that remain unsolved, and revisit them periodically as AI systems become stronger.
roadmap.short: Open challenges on problems that remain unsolved.

submissions.summary: The benchmark, its first task set and the accompanying agent results go to ICML 2027.
The complete task set, environments and evaluation results are submitted to Nature.
submissions.short: The full task set, methodology and results, after ICML.

proposed.label: Proposed
proposed.description: A researcher has proposed this task. It has not yet entered formal scientific review.

under_review.label: Under Review
under_review.description: Automated screening has passed and domain reviewers are assessing scientific value, verifiability and difficulty.

agent_testing.label: Agent Testing
agent_testing.description: The task environment and evaluator are built. Frontier agents are being run to calibrate difficulty and record failure modes.

verified.label: Verified
verified.description: The task, environment and evaluator have been validated under the AI4S-Benchmark evaluation procedure.

released.label: Released
released.description: The task is part of a versioned AI4S-Benchmark release.

criteria.title: Scientific Value
criteria.text: The task represents something researchers in the field genuinely consider meaningful — not difficulty invented purely to confuse an AI.

criteria.title: Verifiable
criteria.text: Correctness can be judged through a script, metric, experimental criterion or explicit scientific evaluation procedure.

criteria.title: Frontier Difficulty
criteria.text: The task remains genuinely challenging for current agents, or involves a workflow whose solution itself constitutes meaningful scientific work.

points.contribution: Contributor organization, review coordination, helping newcomers

roles.name: Contributor
roles.description: Recognized in CONTRIBUTORS.md, the website contributor directory and the relevant release contributor list.

roles.name: Active Contributor
roles.description: A sustained participant across tasks, reviews or maintenance.

roles.name: Core Contributor
roles.description: Demonstrated breadth — for example Task + Review, or Task + Maintain.

roles.name: Maintainer
roles.description: Participates in task acceptance, review organization, contributor management, roadmap and important technical decisions.

credit.committees_note: Scientific areas may form field-specific committees (Area Chair, Committee Members) responsible for organizing reviews and deciding task acceptance in that area. Committees are being formed as the community grows.
credit.authorship_note: Substantive academic contributions may be considered for authorship according to the contribution and release policy. Specific task and review credit remains permanently visible regardless.
